one_month_reasoning: Two events fall in the window. (1) Q3-2026 results. The company has not announced a date. Third-party estimates are Nov 2 (Earnings Whispers [25]) and Nov 4, and Generac reported Q3 2025 on Oct 29, so the print very likely lands before Nov 8. A soft residential quarter is expected: outages ran more than 30% below the long-term baseline in Q2, and the 2026 residential guide assumes a return to baseline [2]. The call should be the first full discussion of the Amazon agreement ($2.4B of 2027-28 deliveries [3]) and of the Sussex/Belvidere ramp [2]. Amazon is, by inference, the 'second hyperscaler' disclosed unnamed in July [1] (press reports [29][30] name it; the Ex. 10.1 recital [52] dates Amazon's Global Purchase Agreement June 24, 2026; no filing states it), so the call should confirm volumes the market has seen rather than reveal a new customer. Earnings-period moves are large in both directions. On the Amazon news the stock went from $175.11 to a $231.89 intraday high on Sep 17 and closed at $207.23 [18]. (2) Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin on the night of Oct 9, after the close [23]. It was forecast days ahead, and the stock rose from $215.20 (Oct 5) to $224.94 (Oct 9) [18], so much of it is likely priced in. It is a single Panhandle storm, not an active season. I set the median at $226, just above spot. The spread is a 50/50 mix of 13% and 21% one-month lognormal sigmas around the stock's usual ~16% monthly vol (56%/3.5), widened for the print. Round 1 cited Q3 estimate revisions from a keyed feed; that is removed.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount is a mix effect that should persist through the horizon, not a call that GNRC will underperform. The peers split into residential-durable and engine names (AOS 14.47x, LII 14.43x, CMI 15.94x) and data-center electrical names (VRT, ETN, NVT, POWL, CAT 27.8-30.8x). Even on the horizon mix, about two-thirds of GNRC's sales are residential or traditional C&I, and residential earns most of the profit (Q2 segment EBITDA $215.4M residential vs $81.5M C&I [1]). Three things keep it there. (a) Residential earnings depend on outages and are volatile (Q2 outages >30% below baseline [2]). (b) Hyperscale business earns lower margins with no above-market price premium [2], and concentration rises: Amazon gets a warrant for 1.69M shares and has no disclosed minimum purchase [3]. (c) Equity risk is high: 5y beta 1.92 [5]. [Citation gate 2026-10-12: peer multiples quoted here are StockAnalysis ratios, which the gate does not accept for peer multiples. reasoning: Facts: Q2-26 sales were $1.17B (+11%), adjusted EPS $2.91 including ~$71M of pretax tariff refunds (~$0.90/share) [1][2]. FY26 margin guidance is 20-21%, including ~1.5 pts of refunds (18.5-19.5% underlying) [1]. Management expects ~$450M of 2026 DC revenue, ~$350M of FCF and capex ~4.5% of sales. The $1.6B DC backlog has $1.35B scheduled for 2027 and nothing for 2028 [2]. Hyperscalers: the first signed in early June and has committed ~$700M for 2027. The second signed June 24, was negotiating 2027-28 volumes, and was expected to be 'at least as big' as the first [1][2]. The Sep 16 8-K gives Amazon $2.4B of expected 2027-28 deliveries, up to $8B in total, and a 1.69M-share warrant at $200.93 with Firm Orders of a redacted minimum (Ex. 10.1 [52]; the 8-K gives no amount [3]). Two press reports say Amazon is that second hyperscaler ([29], [30]); they are not independent (both rest on the 8-K), and the primary support is the Ex. 10.1 recital of a Global Purchase Agreement dated June 24, 2026 [52], an inference. The 8-K does not name it, but the 2027-28 timing matches. I therefore count no separate second-hyperscaler award, which trims my bull case to $325. Round-2 changes after the supervisor's review: (1) EPS base is the openly checkable $12.97 [4] instead of the keyed $12.67. (2) FY28 is re-derived from verified items only: implied FY27 DC $1.84B, FY28 DC $2.44B, revenue $7.30B, EPS $14.56 (+12.3% vs +18% before); the Stocktwits-relayed broker figures are removed. (3) The TIKR investor-day framework is removed from the DCF. (4) GEV and BE are dropped from comps (10 names, median 28.1x). (5) The DCF uses reported net debt $1.064B, valued today and rolled forward at the cost of equity: $138.6 (from $144.4). (6) DCF weight is cut from 30% to 20%. I accept the supervisor's point that 12-month prices follow forward multiples, but keep more DCF weight than its 15% because a 5.24% risk-free rate and a 1.92 beta are real gravity on a stock that has de-rated before. Fair value is $242.9 (from $234.6), 8% above spot and below the $287.78 Street mean [4]. Lane evidence is context, not inputs. A Substack note logged the +18.34% deal day on 3.32x volume [19], which matches the price history [18]. Stocktwits retail sentiment was 'extremely bullish' [20], a contrarian caution. Trade research has large-genset lead times at 18-24 months and $450-600/kW pricing through at least 2027 [24][31]. Sussex job postings back the capacity build [26]. Insider Form 4s are small 10b5-1 sales [28]. Prediction markets give Isaias landfall (resolved) [22] and a thin recession market [21]. Correction to round 1: the Sep 17 intraday high was $231.89, not ~$250 [18]. The ladder is a three-scenario lognormal mixture (bear $150 / 25%, base $240 / 50%, bull $325 / 25%; sigmas 0.35 / 0.25 / 0.31): median ~$236, mean ~$249, overall log-sd ~0.40. That is below the 56% realized vol, which is inflated by the deal-day jump: the Aug-Oct daily closes [18] give 59% annualised with it and 45% without it. Fat tails are kept: P(>= $450) = 4%, P(< $135) = 10%. Limits: keyed feeds (Alpha Vantage, Twelve Data) are no longer cited. One Nasdaq page returned 503. In-lane share is 9 of 31 sources (29%), below the 60% target, because the mandated comps and filings dominate the citation count.
